t: You're looking at the statue of Thomas Becket in St Paul's Churchyard, made in 1970 by Edward Bainbridge Copnall. Becket was Lord Chancellor, then Archbishop of Canterbury from 1162 until his death in 1170. He clashed with King Henry the Second over the rights and privileges of the Church, and was murdered by followers of the king. He is venerated as a saint and martyr. Copnall, the sculptor, was a British artist best known for architectural and decorative work with religious subjects, and he was President of the Royal Society of Sculptors in the sixties.
